PASS-WITH-NOTES — performance/292, final C34 round.

Exact head: f8dd60133f05ebadc443029a5bcece53d5390578, clean detached ../review-292-f8dd601. Round-2 delta reviewed against d398803f7169ef29f136704536205e8c8210ae06; original performance BLOCK was 6f069620dfa17233b28b1a567e6b081776510290. This answers 01a1f922-8d88-73c0-989d-2a04b6ac7290. Static performance verdict, not a deployed-cost or whole-PR functional clearance.

P292-001 repaired in the Live::drop path: the waiters lock, pipe write/flush and answer wait now run on pij-tmux-leave; the caller waits at most TEARDOWN_WAIT (1 s), then kills the owned child and uses the bounded REAP_WAIT (1 s) try_wait phase before deferring reap. A saturated/non-reading pipe can keep the helper alive, not hold that caller's wait indefinitely. The 1+1 s budgets do not bound preexisting ControlClient.release state-lock contention, all Daemon.shutdown worker drainage, OS scheduling, or thread-admission overhead. Reviewer owns focused runtime receipts; performance did not duplicate them.

P292-002 repaired: bounce-rs uses bash SECONDS elapsed checks and absolute /bin/sleep 0.2, with a 30 s graceful drain and a second 5 s drain after SIGKILL. Whole-second sampling and a sleep/scheduling edge qualify the elapsed limit; it is no longer a count of 150 sleeps. If the old PID remains or :7461 is held after draining, no new daemon starts. These PID/port checks are availability brakes: removing them permits more starts, never a different selection policy. Build/install happens before the signal and is outside reconnect-unavailability timing.

R292 identity repair: setup and teardown both require the sole pane's canonical sleep start-command match, not merely one-window/one-pane counts. Teardown preserves a sole nonmatching real-work pane. Later healthy client setup restores destroy-unattached on when only the idle pane remains; it intentionally does not restore it while real work remains. Restoration is setup-triggered, not a new recurring watcher. Raven separately reported an isolated tmux 3.6a fresh-on / forced-off / later-idle-attach-on probe at this exact head; that preliminary result is peer-reported, not a performance-executed test. Performance makes no strict daemon-wide 2 s or automatic no-reconnect restoration claim.

Cost accounting:
- Normal exit: one command over the existing tmux control pipe and one new leave thread, plus fixed fd/channel/queue/quoting work. No OS process launch, no launch-time helper thread.
- Pathological stuck exit: up to TWO new helper threads (leave and deferred reaper), with the existing reply reader potentially surviving until EOF. No global cap across repeated stuck exits; 'one short-lived thread' describes the healthy path only.
- Bounded reap: in-process try_wait checks separated by 5 ms thread sleeps, nominally up to about 200 checks/s per reaping exit during the 1 s budget. This is an exit-only loop, not per-tick/per-seat fleet work; no child process launch per poll.
- Bounce: nominally up to 5 /bin/sleep launches/s per simultaneous draining bounce, only while draining, plus one additional post-drain lsof. Graceful and post-SIGKILL phases are distinct. No daemon steady-state launch-rate change is inferred from this.
- Attach: still one lock open per client start; parent/descriptor metadata, ownership/link-count checks and conditional chmod are in-process. No new per-read launch or recurring poller. SIGTERM adds a one-shot signal/shutdown path, not a timer.
- crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs is unchanged in the final delta. No new daemon child-process launch site was introduced; this does not mean bounce or existing launch sites cost zero.

Named residual F240 (P292-R2-001): reap ignores Builder.spawn failure. If thread admission fails under resource exhaustion, Child is dropped without wait and may later remain unreaped. Static failure-path finding; no induced exhaustion experiment. Prime's C34 ruling, relayed by pij-steady-otter from dee10299...31, explicitly ships it as F240 rather than a blocker; the separate small PR handles the reaper spawn Err. No third review round requested.

Evidence: /tmp/performance-292-final-static-cost.json; final delta artifact://296; exact source sections and unchanged spawn inventory were inspected. No performance-seat builds, tests, stress reruns, reloads, bounces, kills, or product edits. Author's 0/2000 crash results on each tmux version are retained packet evidence, not independently rerun here. Reviewer runtime evidence remains separately attributed.

Holding: performance/292 retained until merge. F238 deployed proof remains owed: same-incarnation old/new spawn and CPU-TIME/RSS windows around a prime-owned bounce, with build duration separated from signal-to-old-gone/new-ready duration. Do not bounce before performance records the old-incarnation baseline.

magicWand: teardown proof should identify caller wait budgets separately from surviving helper lifetimes and thread-admission failure. This review encodes that distinction and the F240 follow-up instead of hiding it behind green tests.
